lead_en: A brush, a stick of ink, a sheet of paper, and a stone. People have written with brush and ink for more than two thousand years and turned writing into an art. Watch a brush write in slow motion, then try it yourself.
lead_zh: 一枝筆、一塊墨、一張紙、一方硯。人們用筆墨寫字已經兩千多年，把寫字變成了藝術。先看毛筆慢動作怎麼寫，再自己動手試試。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with a question about the brush, the characters, or the people who wrote them. A 3D brush writes on Xuan paper in slow motion, one idea at a time, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從一個問題開始：關於毛筆、關於字、或是寫字的人。一枝 3D 毛筆在宣紙上用慢動作寫字，一課只講清楚一件事；再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: At the bottom of every lesson is a practice pad. Write with a mouse, a finger, or a stylus: write slowly for a thick line and quickly for a thin one, just like a real brush. Stroke order follows Taiwan's Ministry of Education standard, and every date, name, and place has been checked against the sources listed on each page.
intro.zh: 每一課下方都有練字板：用滑鼠、手指或觸控筆寫，寫得慢線就粗、寫得快線就細，跟真的毛筆一樣。筆順照教育部的標準；每一個年代、人名、地名都查證過，出處列在每一頁最下方。

units.blurb_en: The four tools on a calligrapher's desk, how a soft brush makes thick and thin lines, the eight basic strokes, and why strokes go in order.
units.blurb_zh: 書桌上的四樣工具、軟軟的毛筆怎麼寫出粗細、八種基本筆畫，以及筆順為什麼有先後。

lessons.title: What Are the Four Treasures of the Study?
lessons.blurb_en: Brush, ink, paper, and inkstone: turn a scholar's desk in 3D, grind ink, drop it on two kinds of paper, and watch a brush write 一 (one) in slow motion. Then write it yourself.
lessons.blurb_zh: 筆、墨、紙、硯：在 3D 裡轉著看讀書人的書桌，磨墨、把墨滴在兩種紙上，再看毛筆慢動作寫出「一」。最後自己寫寫看。
lessons.big_idea_en: Chinese calligraphy needs only four tools: a brush, ink, paper, and an inkstone. Each one has its secrets: brush hair can be soft or springy, ink is made from soot, Xuan paper drinks in ink, and the inkstone is where you grind the ink.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 書法只要四樣工具：筆、墨、紙、硯。每一樣都有學問：筆毛有軟有硬、墨是煙灰做的、宣紙會吸墨、硯台用來磨墨。

lab.title_en: The Four Treasures on a Desk
lab.how_en: Drag to turn the desk, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Tap the brush, the ink stick, the paper, or the inkstone (or use the buttons) to take a closer look at each one. Then choose Write to watch the brush dip into the ink and write 一 (one) in slow motion, from the side, from above, or right next to the tip.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉書桌，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。點一下桌上的毛筆、墨條、紙或硯台（或用右邊的按鈕），就能飛過去近看。最後選「寫一筆」，看毛筆蘸墨、慢動作寫出「一」，可以從側面、正上方或貼近筆尖看。

focus.text_en: The brush, ink, paper, and inkstone are the Four Treasures of the Study. The brush rest, the paperweight, and the water dropper are helpers, and the felt pad under the paper soaks up extra ink. Tap anything on the desk to look closer.
focus.text_zh: 筆、墨、紙、硯就是文房四寶。筆架、紙鎮、水盂是小幫手，紙下面的毛氈會吸掉多餘的墨。點桌上任何一樣東西，就能近看。

focus.text_en: Choose a hair, and the brush presses down on a scrap of paper with the same force each time. Soft goat hair bends the most; springy weasel hair bounces back the fastest. Then check the four virtues of a good brush.
focus.text_zh: 選一種筆毛，毛筆每次都用同樣的力道壓在小紙片上：軟的羊毫彎得最多，有彈性的狼毫彈回最快。再看看好筆的四個條件。

focus.text_en: An ink stick is soot mixed with glue, pressed in a mold, and dried. Grind it in slow circles with a little water on the inkstone, and the water turns black, a little at a time.
focus.text_zh: 墨條是煙灰加膠、壓進模子再晾乾做成的。在硯台上加一點水、慢慢畫圈磨，水就一點一點變黑。

focus.text_en: The same drop of ink falls on raw Xuan paper and on copy paper. Raw Xuan paper drinks in the water, so the ink spreads with soft, fuzzy edges. Copy paper is sized, or coated, so the drop sits on top, shines, and stays small.
focus.text_zh: 同一滴墨落在生宣紙和影印紙上：生宣紙會把水吸進去，墨就暈開，邊緣毛毛的；影印紙上過膠，墨珠停在表面、亮亮的，幾乎不擴散。

focus.text_en: The flat part where you grind is the grinding surface, sometimes called the hill. The deep end is the ink well, or the sea, where the finished ink collects. A water dropper adds just a few drops of water at a time.
focus.text_zh: 磨墨的平面叫硯堂，英文叫它 the hill（山丘）；一頭深下去的地方是硯池，英文叫 the sea（海），磨好的墨流到那裡。水盂一次只加幾滴水。

focus.text_en: The same engine will write every character in this series. Slow it down, pause it, and change the view. The curve shows how hard the brush presses along the stroke.
focus.text_zh: 這個系列每一個字都由同一套寫字引擎來寫。可以放慢、暫停、換角度；下面的曲線是這一筆每個地方壓多重。

virtues.text_en: The hairs come to one fine point.
virtues.text_zh: 筆毛收成一個細細的尖。

virtues.text_en: Pressed flat, the hair tips line up evenly.
virtues.text_zh: 壓扁攤開時，毛尖排得整整齊齊。

virtues.text_en: The tuft is full and round all the way around.
virtues.text_zh: 筆頭飽滿，四周都是圓的。

virtues.text_en: After you press it, it springs back straight.
virtues.text_zh: 壓下去再放開，馬上彈回直直的。

phases.text_en: The tip goes a little to the left, against the way the stroke will go, then the brush presses down to the lower right. The tip is hidden inside the stroke, and the head comes out square.
phases.text_zh: 筆尖先往左逆著走一點，再往右下按：筆尖藏在筆畫裡（藏鋒），起頭方方正正。

phases.text_en: The handle stays upright and the brush moves steadily to the right, a little uphill. The tip runs along the middle of the line, so the stroke is round and full.
phases.text_zh: 筆桿直立，穩穩地往右、稍微往上走；筆尖走在線的中間（中鋒），線條圓潤飽滿。

phases.text_en: Near the end the brush lifts a little, presses down to the lower right again, then turns back to the left and lifts off. The end is rounded, and the tip finishes inside the stroke.
phases.text_zh: 快到終點時先稍微提起，再往右下一按，然後往回收、提筆離紙（回鋒）：收尾圓潤，筆尖收在筆畫裡。

legend.en: White labels: helpers on the desk and parts of each treasure
legend.zh: 白色標籤：桌上的小幫手、各部位的名稱

legend.en: Red lines: the 米 grid printed on practice paper
legend.zh: 紅線：練習紙上的米字格

legend.en: Gold curve: how hard the brush presses along the stroke
legend.zh: 金色曲線：這一筆每個地方壓多重

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Sizes are roughly real: the brush is about 26 centimeters long, and the grid on the paper is 26 centimeters wide. How far ink spreads, how fast the water turns black, and how much each kind of hair bends are illustrations, not measurements. The stroke 一 is hand-drawn as a centerline with a pressure for every point.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。大小大約照真的：毛筆約 26 公分長，紙上的格子 26 公分寬。墨暈開多遠、水變黑多快、各種筆毛彎多少，都是示意，不是量測。「一」這一筆是自己手繪的中心線，每一點都有壓力。

paras: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing. In Chinese calligraphy, people write characters with a soft brush and black ink, and they need only four tools: a brush, an ink stick, paper, and an inkstone. Together these are called the Four Treasures of the Study, because for centuries they sat on the desk in a scholar's study. People have written with brushes for a very long time. The oldest brush ever found came from a tomb near Changsha and is more than 2,200 years old.

The brush is a bundle of animal hair tied into a point and fixed to a bamboo handle. Soft white goat hair holds a lot of ink and makes round, gentle lines. Springy brown hair from the tail of a weasel makes sharp, strong lines. In Chinese it is called “wolf hair,” but it usually comes from a weasel. Many brushes mix the two kinds. A good brush has four virtues: its tip is sharp, its hairs are even, its body is round, and it springs back after you press it.

An ink stick looks like a small black bar, but it is made from soot. Makers burn pine wood or oil, collect the fine black soot, mix it with glue, and press it into molds to dry. To make liquid ink, you put a few drops of water on the inkstone and rub the stick in slow circles. Bit by bit, the soot comes off, and the water turns black. Grinding takes time, so many people today use bottled ink, but grinding is also a calm way to get ready to write.

Calligraphers often write on Xuan paper, which is named after Xuanzhou in Anhui Province, China. It is made by hand from the bark of the blue sandalwood tree and rice straw. Raw Xuan paper drinks in water, so a drop of ink spreads out with soft edges, and the paper shows every move of the brush. Copy paper is different. It is sized, or coated, so the water cannot soak in, and the ink sits on top. In Taiwan, the town of Puli has made handmade paper since the Japanese era.

The inkstone is a flat piece of fine, hard stone. Its surface is smooth but a little rough, just enough to grind the ink stick quickly. The flat part where you grind is called the hill, and the deep part at one end is called the sea, where the finished ink collects. Some of the most famous inkstones are Duan inkstones, carved from purple stone near Zhaoqing in Guangdong Province, an area that was called Duanzhou in the Tang dynasty.

Calligraphy is not only for experts or for grandparents. In Taiwan, students begin writing with a brush in third or fourth grade, and many people write spring couplets for the Lunar New Year. You do not even need ink to start: a brush dipped in clean water can practice on old newspaper or on a water-writing cloth, where the marks fade as they dry. In this lesson, first watch the 3D brush write the character 一 (one) in slow motion. Then try writing it yourself on the practice pad.
paras_zh: 書法是把字寫得美的藝術。寫中國書法要用柔軟的毛筆和黑色的墨，而且只需要四樣工具：筆、墨條、紙和硯台。這四樣合稱「文房四寶」，因為幾百年來它們就擺在讀書人書房的桌上。人們用毛筆寫字已經很久很久了：目前找到最古老的毛筆，出土於長沙附近的一座墓，已經有兩千兩百多年。
毛筆是一束動物的毛，紮成尖尖的形狀，裝在竹子做的筆桿上。軟軟的白色羊毛（羊毫）吸得住很多墨，寫出來的線條圓潤柔和；黃鼠狼尾巴上有彈性的褐色毛，寫出來的線條銳利有力。這種毛中文叫「狼毫」，其實通常來自黃鼠狼。很多毛筆把兩種毛混在一起（兼毫）。好的毛筆有四個條件：筆尖要尖、毛要齊、筆肚要圓、壓下去要能彈回來（尖、齊、圓、健）。
墨條看起來像一根黑色的小棒子，其實是用煙灰做的。做墨的人燒松木或油，收集細細的黑色煙灰，加上膠拌勻，壓進模子裡晾乾。要變成墨汁，就在硯台上滴幾滴水，拿墨條慢慢畫圈磨：煙灰一點一點磨下來，水就變黑了。磨墨很花時間，所以今天很多人用瓶裝的墨汁；不過磨墨也是寫字前讓心安靜下來的好方法。
書法家常寫在宣紙上。宣紙的名字來自中國安徽的宣州，是用青檀樹的樹皮和稻草手工做成的。生宣紙會把水吸進去，所以一滴墨會暈開、邊緣柔柔的，筆的每一個動作都看得出來。影印紙就不一樣了：它上過膠，水滲不進去，墨就停在表面。在台灣，埔里從日治時代就開始做手工紙。
硯台是一塊扁平、細緻又堅硬的石頭。它的表面光滑，卻又帶一點點粗，剛好能把墨條很快磨下來。磨墨的平面叫「硯堂」，英文叫它「山丘」（the hill）；一頭深下去的地方叫「硯池」，英文叫它「海」（the sea），磨好的墨就流到那裡。最有名的硯台之一是端硯，用廣東肇慶附近的紫色石頭雕成；這一帶在唐代叫端州。
書法不是只有專家或爺爺奶奶在寫。在台灣，學生在三、四年級就開始學寫毛筆字，過農曆年時也有很多人寫春聯。開始練習甚至不需要墨：毛筆蘸清水，就能在舊報紙或水寫布上練習，水痕乾了就消失。這一課，先看 3D 毛筆用慢動作寫出「一」，再到練字板上自己寫寫看。

parts.text_en: Press three kinds of brushes with the same force. Which bends the most, and which springs back the fastest?
parts.text_zh: 用同樣的力道壓三種毛筆：哪一種彎得最多？哪一種彈回最快？

parts.meta_en: Soot and glue, ground with water
parts.text_en: Grind the ink stick in circles on the inkstone and watch the water turn black.
parts.text_zh: 拿墨條在硯台上畫圈磨，看水慢慢變黑。

parts.meta_en: Raw Xuan paper vs. copy paper
parts.meta_zh: 生宣紙 vs. 影印紙

parts.text_zh: 把同一滴墨滴在兩種紙上，比比看暈開多遠。

drops.en: A Drop of Ink on Different Papers
drops.lead_en: Choose thick, medium, or light ink, and the same drop falls on four papers at once. The number shows how many times wider the spot has grown than the drop. It is an illustration of how each paper takes in water, not a lab measurement.
drops.lead_zh: 選濃墨、中墨或淡墨，同一滴墨同時落在四種紙上。數字是墨跡比剛落下時寬了幾倍。這是依照各種紙吸水的情形畫的示意，不是實驗量測。

papers.text_en: Not sized, so it drinks water fast. The ink spreads with fuzzy edges and a pale ring of water.
papers.text_zh: 沒上膠，吸水很快：墨暈開，邊緣毛毛的，外圈還有一圈淡淡的水痕。

papers.text_en: Brushed with alum, so it takes in much less water. Good for fine, careful painting.
papers.text_zh: 刷過明礬，吸水少得多，適合畫細緻的工筆畫。

papers.text_en: Soft and thirsty, but uneven. Great for practicing with clean water.
papers.text_zh: 軟軟的、很會吸水，但不均勻。用清水練字很適合。

papers.text_en: Sized and smooth. The drop sits on top, shines, and takes a long time to dry.
papers.text_zh: 上過膠、很光滑：墨珠停在表面、亮亮的，很久才乾。

pad.lead_en: Trace the faint red 一 with a mouse, a finger, or a stylus. Move slowly for a thick line and quickly for a thin one; with a stylus, pressing harder makes the line thicker. Tap Watch the demo to see the brush write it first, and save your best one as a picture.
pad.lead_zh: 用滑鼠、手指或觸控筆，描寫淡紅色的「一」。寫得慢線就粗，寫得快線就細；用觸控筆時，越用力越粗。先按「看示範」看毛筆怎麼寫，寫得滿意就存成圖片。

tips.en: Start by pressing down to the lower right, like the brush in the model.
tips.zh: 起筆先往右下按，就像模型裡的毛筆。

tips.en: Move at a steady speed through the middle, a little uphill.
tips.zh: 中間用穩定的速度走，稍微往上斜。

tips.en: At the end, slow down, press, and lift.
tips.zh: 最後放慢、按一下，再提起來。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of the Four Treasures · 四寶的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Four places, a famous name, Taiwan's paper, and an old saying
culture_cards.title_zh: 四個產地、一個名稱、台灣的紙、一句成語
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories behind the tools on the desk.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 書桌上這幾樣工具背後的四個小故事。

cards.en: Where the famous treasures come from
cards.body_en: The best-known treasures are named after the places that made them famous. Hu brushes come from Huzhou in Zhejiang, where the town of Shanlian still makes them by hand. Hui ink comes from old Huizhou in Anhui, and She County still makes it. Xuan paper is named after Xuanzhou in Anhui and is made in Jing County; in 2009 the craft was added to UNESCO's list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Duan inkstones are carved near Zhaoqing in Guangdong, which was called Duanzhou in the Tang dynasty.
cards.body_zh: 最有名的四寶，常用產地來稱呼。湖筆出自浙江湖州，善璉鎮至今還在手工製筆；徽墨出自安徽古徽州，歙縣至今仍在製墨；宣紙因安徽宣州得名，產在涇縣，2009 年宣紙傳統製作技藝列入聯合國教科文組織的人類非物質文化遺產代表作名錄；端硯雕自廣東肇慶附近，肇慶在唐代叫端州。

cards.en: Where “the Four Treasures of the Study” comes from
cards.body_en: Wenfang (文房) means a scholar's study, the room for reading and writing. In the late 900s, Su Yijian, an official of the Song dynasty, wrote a whole book about the four tools, the Wenfang Sipu (Four Records of the Study): two parts on brushes, and one part each on inkstones, ink, and paper. Another Song writer, Ye Mengde, wrote down a saying of his time: “Shezhou has the Four Treasures of the Study,” meaning brush, ink, paper, and inkstone. In 1121, Shezhou was renamed Huizhou, the home of Hui ink.
cards.body_zh: 「文房」是讀書人的書房，讀書寫字的地方。北宋官員蘇易簡在十世紀後半寫了一整本講這四樣工具的書《文房四譜》：筆兩卷，硯、墨、紙各一卷。宋代的葉夢得也記下當時的說法：「世言歙州有文房四寶，謂筆、墨、紙、硯也。」歙州在 1121 年改名徽州，也就是徽墨的故鄉。

cards.k: Made in Taiwan · 台灣的紙
cards.body_en: Puli, near the geographic center of Taiwan, is known for its clean water, and papermakers need clean water. Handmade papermaking skills from Japan and China came to Puli during the Japanese era, and after World War II, through the 1960s and 1970s, Puli's handmade paper enjoyed a short export boom. From the 1980s the industry shrank, as many mills closed or moved to mainland China or Southeast Asia, and after the 1999 earthquake even fewer remained. Some of the mills still working now welcome visitors, who can watch paper being made and try making a sheet themselves.
cards.body_zh: 埔里位在台灣地理中心附近，以水質純淨聞名，而造紙最需要好水。日治時期，日本和中國的手工造紙技術傳進埔里；二戰後到 1960、70 年代，埔里的手工紙曾短暫外銷興盛。1980 年代起產業逐漸萎縮，許多紙廠關門，或搬到中國大陸、東南亞設廠；1999 年九二一地震後，紙廠又更少了。還在做紙的紙廠，有些開放參觀，可以看師傅抄紙，也能自己動手做一張。

cards.en: Three fen into the wood: 入木三分
cards.body_en: An old story says that Wang Xizhi, the great calligrapher of the Eastern Jin dynasty, once wrote on a wooden board for a ceremony. Later, when workers shaved the board to write on it again, they found his ink had soaked three fen deep into the wood (a fen is a small old unit of length). Today 入木三分 describes powerful brushwork, and also a comment or description that goes deep and gets right to the point.
cards.body_zh: 相傳東晉書法家王羲之曾在祭祀用的木板上寫字，後來工人要把木板削掉重寫，發現墨跡滲進木頭有三分深（分是古代很小的長度單位）。今天「入木三分」用來形容筆力強勁，也比喻評論深刻中肯、描寫生動逼真。

myths.myth_en: You need bottled ink to write calligraphy.
myths.myth_zh: 寫毛筆字一定要用墨汁。
myths.fact_en: For centuries, ink was ground fresh from an ink stick on an inkstone. Bottled ink is a modern shortcut that many classes use, and beginners can even practice with plain water on newspaper or a water-writing cloth.
myths.fact_zh: 幾百年來，墨都是拿墨條在硯台上現磨的。瓶裝墨汁是現代的方便做法，很多課堂都用；初學的人甚至可以只用清水，在報紙或水寫布上練習。

myths.myth_en: Xuan paper is just ordinary white paper.
myths.fact_en: Xuan paper is made by hand from tree bark and rice straw. Raw Xuan paper is not sized, so it drinks in water and makes ink spread; copy paper is sized and smooth, so ink sits on top. The English name “rice paper” is misleading, too: the fibers come from bark and straw, not from rice grains.
myths.fact_zh: 宣紙是用樹皮和稻草手工做的。生宣紙沒上膠，會吸水、讓墨暈開；影印紙上過膠又光滑，墨停在表面。英文常說的「rice paper（米紙）」也容易誤會：纖維來自樹皮和稻草，不是米粒。

myths.myth_en: The softer the brush, the easier it is to write.
myths.fact_en: Soft goat hair holds lots of ink, but it bends a lot and springs back slowly, so it is hard to control. Springier weasel-hair or mixed-hair brushes are often easier for beginners.
myths.fact_zh: 軟的羊毫吸墨多，可是彎得多、彈回得慢，比較難控制。有彈性的狼毫或兼毫，對初學者常常比較好寫。

myths.fact_en: In Taiwan, students start writing with a brush in third or fourth grade as part of their Chinese lessons, and people of all ages write spring couplets for the Lunar New Year.
myths.fact_zh: 在台灣，學生三、四年級就在國語課學寫毛筆字；過農曆年寫春聯的，也是男女老少都有。

tricks.body_en: Four tools on one desk: the Four Treasures of the Study.
tricks.body_zh: 四樣工具一張桌：文房四寶。

tricks.body_en: A good brush comes to a point, lines up evenly, stays round, and springs back.
tricks.body_zh: 好筆四個條件：筆尖尖、毛整齊、筆肚圓、有彈性。

tricks.body_en: A few drops of water, small circles, and patience make dark ink.
tricks.body_zh: 幾滴水、畫小圓、有耐心，墨就黑了。

tricks.title_en: Raw paper drinks, copy paper doesn't
tricks.title_zh: 生宣會喝水，影印紙不喝
tricks.body_en: On raw Xuan paper, ink spreads; on sized paper, it stays put.
tricks.body_zh: 墨在生宣紙上會暈開，在上過膠的紙上停在原地。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: Inkstones are heavy stone. Carry them with two hands, and set them down gently.
safety.zh: 硯台是石頭，很重：用兩隻手拿，輕輕放下。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Old newspaper or a water-writing cloth

steps.en: Dip the brush in the water, then wipe it on the edge of the cup so it is wet but not dripping.
steps.zh: 毛筆蘸水，在杯緣刮一刮，讓它濕濕的但不會滴水。

steps.en: Hold the brush straight up, like the brush in the 3D model.
steps.zh: 像 3D 模型裡的毛筆一樣，把筆桿拿直。

steps.en: Write a row of horizontal lines from left to right. Press down at the start, move steadily, then press and lift at the end.
steps.zh: 由左到右寫一排橫線：起筆往下按、中間穩穩地走、最後按一下再提起。

steps.en: Write one line slowly and one line quickly. Which is thicker? Watch the water marks fade as they dry, then write again in the same place.
steps.zh: 一條慢慢寫、一條快快寫：哪一條比較粗？看水痕乾掉慢慢消失，再在同一個地方重寫。

activities.tip_en: Water writing is clean and cheap, and you can repeat it as many times as you like, so it works well for a whole class. Newspaper soaks up water a bit like raw Xuan paper, so it also shows how ink would spread.
activities.tip_zh: 用清水練字乾淨又省錢，想寫幾次就寫幾次，很適合全班一起練。報紙吸水的樣子有點像生宣紙，也看得出墨會怎麼暈開。

activities.title_en: The Ink-Grinding Race: How Many Circles Make Black Ink?
activities.title_zh: 磨墨比賽：磨幾圈水才夠黑？

materials.en: For each team: an inkstone, an ink stick, and a water dropper or a small spoon
materials.zh: 每一組：一個硯台、一條墨條、一個水盂或小湯匙

materials.en: Strips of white paper (raw Xuan paper if you have it)
A record sheet and a pencil
materials.zh: 一張紀錄表和一枝鉛筆

materials.en: Old newspaper to cover the desks

steps.en: Every team puts the same amount of water on the grinding surface, for example five drops.
steps.zh: 每一組在硯堂上放一樣多的水，例如 5 滴。

steps.en: One student grinds in small, slow circles, pressing gently, while a teammate counts the circles.
steps.zh: 一個人輕輕地、慢慢地畫小圓磨墨，隊友數圈數。

steps.en: Every 20 circles, dab a little ink onto a paper strip and write the number of circles beside it.
steps.zh: 每磨 20 圈，在紙條上點一點墨，旁邊寫上圈數。

steps.en: Stop at 100 circles. Line up the strips from every team and compare: whose ink got darkest? Did grinding faster or pressing harder help?
steps.zh: 磨到 100 圈就停。把各組的紙條排在一起比較：誰的墨最黑？磨得快、壓得重有沒有幫助？

activities.tip_en: An old saying goes: grind ink as gently as a sick man, and hold the brush as firmly as a strong man. Pressing hard makes rough, gritty ink. After grinding, wipe the ink stick dry so it does not stick to the stone or crack.
activities.tip_zh: 有句老話說：「磨墨如病夫，執筆如壯士。」用力壓反而磨出粗粗的墨。磨完要把墨條擦乾，免得黏在硯上或裂開。

lessons.title: How Does a Brush Make Thick and Thin Lines?
lessons.title_zh: 一枝毛筆怎麼寫出粗細？
lessons.blurb_en: A brush's tip is soft: press down for a thick line, lift up for a thin one. Control the pressure of a 3D brush yourself, compare the center tip with the side tip, slow down every part of 十 (ten), and see how your own press-and-lift curve compares.
lessons.blurb_zh: 毛筆的筆鋒是軟的：往下按線就粗，往上提線就細。自己控制 3D 毛筆壓多重、比較中鋒和側鋒、把「十」的每一段放慢看，再看看你的提按曲線像不像示範。
lessons.big_idea_en: The biggest difference between a brush and a ballpoint pen is the soft tip. Press down, and the hairs spread for a thick line; lift up, and they gather for a thin one. The beauty of calligraphy lives in the rhythm of pressing and lifting, and it starts with holding the brush upright.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 毛筆和原子筆最大的不同：筆鋒是軟的。往下按，筆毛散開線就粗；往上提，筆毛收攏線就細。書法的美就在提與按的節奏，而這要從把筆拿直開始。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. In Press and lift, the brush crosses the paper row by row while you decide how hard it presses: drag the slider, or choose a pattern. In Center or side tip, the same line is written two ways. In Writing 十, slow down the start, the middle, and the finish of each stroke. Change the view with Side, Top, or Tip.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。「提按」：毛筆一行一行往右寫，壓多重由你決定——拉滑桿，或選一種節奏。「中鋒與側鋒」：同一條線用兩種方法寫。「寫十」：把每一筆的起筆、行筆、收筆放慢看。用「側面、正上方、貼近筆尖」換角度。

modes.text_en: The brush moves at the same speed the whole time. Only the pressure changes, and that is enough to make the line thin, thick, or anything in between. Watch the hairs spread when it presses and gather when it lifts.
modes.text_zh: 毛筆一直用同樣的速度走，只有壓的力道在變，就足以讓線條變細、變粗。看筆毛按下去時散開、提起來時收攏。

modes.text_en: With the handle upright, the tip runs along the middle of the line: the center tip, round and full. With the handle leaning, the tip slides along one edge: the side tip, flat, with one sharp edge and one dry, rough edge.
modes.text_zh: 筆桿直立，筆尖走在線的中間：中鋒，線條圓潤飽滿。筆桿斜了，筆尖貼著一邊走：側鋒，線條扁平，一邊齊、一邊乾乾毛毛的。

modes.text_en: 十 has two strokes: the horizontal first, then the vertical. Pick a stroke and a part to replay it at quarter speed. The curve shows how hard the brush presses along the stroke.
modes.text_zh: 「十」有兩筆：先橫後豎。選一筆、選一段，用四分之一的速度重播；曲線是這一筆每個地方壓多重。

phases.text_en: Hide the tip: it moves a little to the left, against the way the stroke will go, then the brush presses down to the lower right. The head of the stroke comes out square.
phases.text_zh: 藏鋒：筆尖先往左逆著走一點，再往右下按，起頭方方正正。

phases.text_en: Lift a little and move steadily to the right, slightly uphill, with the tip in the middle of the line.
phases.text_zh: 稍微提起，穩穩地往右、稍微往上走，筆尖保持在線的中間。

phases.text_en: Lift slightly, press down to the lower right, then turn the tip back to the left and lift off: the tip returns inside the stroke.
phases.text_zh: 先輕輕提，再往右下一按，然後筆尖往左回收、提筆離紙（回鋒）。

phases.text_en: Hide the tip again: it goes up a little first, then turns and presses down to the lower right.
phases.text_zh: 一樣藏鋒：筆尖先往上逆入一點，再轉往右下按。

phases.text_en: Move straight down at an even speed, keeping the tip in the middle so the line stays round and full.
phases.text_zh: 用平均的速度直直往下走，筆尖在中間，線條圓潤飽滿。

phases.text_en: A hanging needle: keep moving down while you lift a little at a time, until the tip leaves the paper in a fine point.
phases.text_zh: 懸針：一邊往下走、一邊慢慢提起，直到筆尖離開紙面，收成細細的尖。

legend.en: Teal labels: what the brush is doing right now
legend.zh: 青色標籤：毛筆現在在做什麼

legend.en: Gold-edged labels: the line width and the two kinds of tip
legend.zh: 金框標籤：線寬、兩種筆鋒

legend.en: Red lines: the 米 grid (Writing 十)
Gold curve: how hard the brush presses along the stroke
legend.zh: 金色曲線：這一筆每個地方壓多重

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Sizes are roughly real: the brush is about 26 centimeters long, and the grid is 26 centimeters wide, so one thousandth of the grid is 0.26 millimeters; line widths use the same rule as the practice pad. In the side tip, the handle leans about 24 degrees and the ink is drawn hair by hair; real dry-brush streaks depend on the ink, the paper, and the speed. The strokes of 十 are hand-drawn as centerlines with a pressure for every point.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。大小大約照真的：毛筆約 26 公分長，格子 26 公分寬，所以格子的千分之一是 0.26 公釐；線寬和練字板用同一個算法。側鋒時筆桿斜約 24°，墨一根筆毛一根筆毛地畫；真的飛白要看墨、紙和速度。「十」的兩筆是自己手繪的中心線，每一點都有壓力。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. Stroke order follows the Ministry of Education's Stroke Order of Standard Chinese Characters website. · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；筆順依教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》。

paras: Draw a line with a ballpoint pen, and it is the same width from beginning to end. Draw a line with a brush, and it can be as thin as a hair in one place and as wide as your finger in another. The secret is the soft tip. When you press the brush down, the hairs spread out, and the line gets thicker. When you lift it up, the hairs come back together, and the line gets thinner.

Calligraphers call these two movements pressing and lifting. A good line is not pressed the same way from end to end. In a horizontal stroke, the brush presses down at the start, moves a little lighter through the middle, and presses again near the end. This rhythm of pressing and lifting gives a stroke its life, a bit like the beat in a piece of music.

Every stroke has three parts: the start, the middle, and the finish. In regular script, the tip often starts by moving a little in the opposite direction, so that it is hidden inside the stroke. This is called hiding the tip. At the end, the brush can turn back on itself, or it can lift slowly until the line ends in a fine point, like a needle hanging down.

Watch where the tip goes. When the handle stays upright, the tip runs along the middle of the line. This is called the center tip, and it makes lines that look round and full. When the handle leans, the tip slides along one edge, and the line turns flat, with one sharp side and one rough side. This is the side tip.

To keep the tip in the middle, hold the brush upright. A traditional grip, often traced to Lu Xisheng of the Tang dynasty, gives each of the five fingers a job. The thumb, the index finger, and the middle finger hold the handle from both sides, the ring finger pushes back from behind, and the little finger supports the ring finger. Keep your fingers firm but your palm hollow, as if you were holding an egg.

Speed matters, too. When the brush moves slowly, more ink soaks into the paper and the line grows thicker. When it moves quickly, the line becomes thinner and drier. In this lesson, slow down the 3D brush to watch pressing and lifting up close. Then write 十 (ten) on the practice pad: first the horizontal stroke, then the vertical one. The pad will compare your press-and-lift curve with the brush's.
paras_zh: 用原子筆畫一條線，從頭到尾都一樣寬。用毛筆畫一條線，有的地方細得像頭髮，有的地方寬得像手指。祕密就在軟軟的筆鋒：把筆往下按，筆毛散開，線就變粗；往上提，筆毛收攏，線就變細。
書法家把這兩個動作叫做「按」和「提」。好的線條不會從頭到尾壓得一樣重。寫一筆橫的時候，起筆往下按，中間稍微輕一點地走過去，快到終點時再按一次。這種提與按的節奏讓筆畫有了生命，有點像音樂裡的拍子。
每一筆都有三個部分：起筆、行筆、收筆。寫楷書時，筆尖常常先往相反的方向走一點，讓筆尖藏在筆畫裡，這叫「藏鋒」。到了終點，毛筆可以往回收（回鋒），也可以一邊走一邊慢慢提起，讓線條收成細細的尖，像一根懸著的針（懸針）。
注意筆尖走在哪裡。筆桿直立的時候，筆尖走在線的中間，這叫「中鋒」，寫出來的線條圓潤飽滿。筆桿斜了，筆尖就貼著一邊滑過去，線條變得扁平，一邊整齊、一邊粗糙，這叫「側鋒」。
要讓筆尖保持在中間，就要把筆拿直。有一種傳統的拿法，常說是唐代陸希聲傳下來的，讓五根手指各有工作：大拇指、食指、中指從兩邊拿住筆桿，無名指從後面頂住，小指托住無名指。手指要實，掌心要虛，好像手裡握著一顆蛋（指實掌虛）。
速度也有關係。毛筆走得慢，比較多的墨滲進紙裡，線就變粗；走得快，線就變細、也比較乾。這一課，先把 3D 毛筆放慢，近看提和按；再到練字板上寫「十」：先寫橫，再寫豎。練字板會把你的提按曲線和毛筆的拿來比較。
questions: Why can one brush make both thick and thin lines?
What are the three parts of a stroke, and what does hiding the tip mean?
What is the difference between the center tip and the side tip?
answers: Its tip is soft. When you press it down, the hairs spread and the line gets thicker; when you lift it up, the hairs gather and the line gets thinner.
The start, the middle, and the finish. Hiding the tip means the tip first moves a little in the opposite direction, so it stays hidden inside the stroke.

With the center tip, the handle is upright and the tip runs along the middle of the line, so the line is round and full. With the side tip, the handle leans and the tip slides along one edge, so the line is flat, with one sharp side and one rough side.

vocab.ex: Press the button to start the machine.
vocab.exzh: 按下按鈕讓機器開始運轉。

vocab.ex: Please lift the box carefully; it is heavy.
vocab.exzh: 請小心地把箱子提起來，它很重。

vocab.ex: We clapped our hands to the rhythm of the song.
vocab.exzh: 我們跟著歌的節奏拍手。

vocab.ex: The tip of my pencil broke during the test.
vocab.exzh: 考試時我的鉛筆尖斷了。

vocab.ex: Keep your back upright when you sit at your desk.
vocab.exzh: 坐在書桌前時，背要挺直。

vocab.ex: A tennis coach can help you find the right grip.
vocab.exzh: 網球教練可以幫你找到正確的握拍方式。

vocab.exzh: 那棵老樹裡面是空的，有貓頭鷹住在裡面。

options: The hairs spread and the line gets thicker.
The hairs gather and the line gets thinner.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: One line goes thin, thick, thin
parts.meta_zh: 一條線由細變粗再變細
parts.text_en: The brush keeps the same speed; only the pressure swells and fades.
parts.text_zh: 毛筆速度不變，只有力道慢慢加重又減輕。

parts.text_en: Watch the hairs spread and gather three times in one line.
parts.text_zh: 一條線裡，看筆毛散開、收攏三次。

parts.meta_zh: 筆桿直立 vs. 筆桿斜
parts.text_en: Write the same line twice and compare the edges from the top view.
parts.text_zh: 同一條線寫兩次，用正上方的角度比較邊緣。

parts.meta_en: The end of 十's vertical stroke
parts.text_en: Watch the brush lift a little at a time until the line ends in a point.
parts.text_zh: 看毛筆一點一點提起，直到線條收成尖。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then choose Writing 十 and replay each part of each stroke at quarter speed.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 再選「寫十」，把每一筆的每一段用四分之一的速度重播。

hold.zh: 五根手指，一枝直立的筆
hold.lead_en: A traditional grip gives each finger one job and names it with one character. It is often traced to Lu Xisheng of the Tang dynasty and is known as the five-character method.
hold.lead_zh: 傳統的執筆法讓每根手指負責一件事，每件事用一個字來說，常說是唐代陸希聲傳下來的「五字執筆法」：擫、押、鉤、格、抵。

fingers.text_en: Presses the handle from the inside, tilted slightly upward.
fingers.text_zh: 大拇指上節貼住筆桿內側，稍微往上斜。

fingers.text_en: Presses from the outside, so the thumb and index finger hold the handle between them.
fingers.text_zh: 食指從外側壓住筆桿，和大拇指一內一外夾住。

fingers.text_en: Curls like a hook around the outside and pulls inward.
fingers.text_zh: 中指彎成鉤，鉤住筆桿外側往內用力。

fingers.text_en: Pushes back from the inside with the edge of the nail, balancing the middle finger.
fingers.text_zh: 無名指以指甲與肉相接處從內側頂住，擋住中指往內的力。

fingers.text_en: Rests against the ring finger to support it.
fingers.text_zh: 小指緊靠無名指，幫它托住。

checks.en: Fingers firm, palm hollow, as if you were holding an egg.
checks.zh: 指實掌虛，掌心好像握著一顆蛋。

checks.en: Wrist and arm stay loose, so the whole arm can move the brush.
checks.zh: 手腕、手臂放鬆，讓整隻手臂帶動毛筆。

pad.en: Write 十 and compare your curve
pad.lead_en: Trace the faint red 十: first the horizontal stroke, then the vertical one. Move slowly for thick and quickly for thin, or press harder with a stylus. After each stroke, the chart shows your press-and-lift curve in blue over the brush's curve in gold.
pad.lead_zh: 描寫淡紅色的「十」：先寫橫，再寫豎。寫得慢線就粗、寫得快線就細，用觸控筆就越用力越粗。每寫完一筆，圖上會用藍線畫出你的提按曲線，疊在毛筆示範的金色曲線上。

tips.en: Stroke 1 first: the horizontal, from left to right.
tips.zh: 先寫第 1 筆：橫，由左到右。

tips.en: Then the vertical, from top to bottom; lift slowly at the end for a fine point.
tips.zh: 再寫豎，由上往下，最後慢慢提起成尖。

tips.en: Check the chart: did you press at the start and lift at the end?
tips.zh: 看看圖：起筆有沒有按、收筆有沒有提？

links_head.en: From the tools to the eight strokes

links.en: What Are the Four Treasures of the Study?
links.note_en: Goat, mixed, and weasel hair: which brush bends the most? Watch the same brush press down on paper.
links.note_zh: 羊毫、兼毫、狼毫：哪一種彎得最多？看同一枝筆按在紙上。

links.en: Can One Character Teach You Every Stroke?
links.zh: 永字八法：一個字學會所有筆畫？
links.note_en: The character 永 (forever) holds the eight basic strokes of regular script. Next time, the brush writes them one by one.
links.note_zh: 「永」這一個字裡就有楷書的八種基本筆畫。下一課，毛筆一筆一筆寫給你看。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Sayings About the Brush · 關於筆的成語
culture_cards.title_en: An upright heart, iron strokes, strength through paper, and dancing dragons
culture_cards.title_zh: 心正筆正、鐵畫銀鉤、力透紙背、筆走龍蛇
culture_cards.lead_en: Four sayings about writing with a brush, and the stories behind them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四句形容寫字的成語，和它們背後的故事。

cards.en: An upright heart, an upright brush
cards.body_en: The Old Book of Tang records that Emperor Muzong once asked the calligrapher Liu Gongquan how to use the brush perfectly. Liu answered, “Using the brush depends on the heart. When the heart is upright, the brush is upright.” The emperor's face changed: he understood that Liu was giving him advice through calligraphy. Today 心正筆正 also means that an honest heart leads to honest actions.
cards.body_zh: 《舊唐書》記載，唐穆宗問書法家柳公權，筆要怎麼用才能寫到最好。柳公權回答：「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」穆宗臉色一變，明白柳公權是藉著書法在勸他。今天「心正筆正」也比喻內心公正，做事就正直。

cards.body_en: The Tang calligrapher Ouyang Xun wrote in his essay On Using the Brush that good strokes are “firm like iron strokes, graceful like silver hooks.” A children's classic, Youxue Qionglin, later used the words for Wang Xizhi's writing. Today 鐵畫銀鉤 praises calligraphy that is both strong and beautiful.
cards.body_zh: 唐代書法家歐陽詢在〈用筆論〉裡說，好的筆畫「剛則鐵畫，媚若銀鉤」：剛勁像鐵、柔美像銀。後來的童蒙書《幼學瓊林》用它來形容王羲之的字。今天「鐵畫銀鉤」用來稱讚書法剛柔並濟。

cards.en: Strength through the back of the paper
cards.body_en: The saying comes from Yan Zhenqing's notes on the brush methods he learned from Zhang Xu: when the writing is strong, its force seems to reach right through to the back of the paper. Today 力透紙背 praises powerful calligraphy, and also writing whose ideas are deep and strong. Strength here means control, not crushing the brush.
cards.body_zh: 這句話出自唐代顏真卿記錄張旭（張長史）筆法的〈張長史十二意筆法記〉：寫字時運筆的力量好像穿透到紙的背面。今天「力透紙背」形容書法遒勁有力，也形容文章立意深刻。這裡的「力」是控制，不是把筆壓扁。

cards.en: The brush runs like dragons and snakes
cards.body_en: The Song poet Shi Xiaoyou praised a friend with the line “筆走龍蛇” in one of his ci poems: the brush moves as freely as dragons and snakes. Today it describes writing or calligraphy that flows freely and skillfully. You will see this kind of movement in running and cursive script later in this series.
cards.body_zh: 宋代詞人石孝友在〈滿庭芳．上張紫微〉裡用「筆走龍蛇」稱讚對方：筆像龍蛇一樣自在地遊走。今天用來形容文筆揮灑自如、書法優美熟練。這個系列後面的行書、草書，就看得到這種動感。

myths.myth_en: Thick lines need a thick brush.
myths.fact_en: One brush can make both. Press it down and the hairs spread; lift it and they gather. In this lesson's model, the same brush makes lines from under 2 millimeters to about 3 centimeters wide.
myths.fact_zh: 同一枝筆就做得到：往下按，筆毛散開；往上提，筆毛收攏。在這一課的模型裡，同一枝筆畫得出不到 2 公釐、到大約 3 公分寬的線。

myths.fact_en: Strength comes from control: pressing and lifting at the right moments. Crushing the brush squashes the hairs, makes blobs, and can split the tip.
myths.fact_zh: 有力來自控制：在對的時候按、在對的時候提。把筆壓扁，筆毛會擠成一團、墨跡變成一坨，筆尖也可能分岔。

myths.myth_en: You hold a brush the same way as a pencil.
myths.fact_en: A brush is held upright, often with all five fingers, and the palm stays hollow. A pencil-style grip tilts the handle, so the tip slides to one side and the line turns flat.
myths.fact_zh: 毛筆要拿直，常用五根手指，掌心是空的。像拿鉛筆那樣斜斜地拿，筆尖會偏到一邊，線就變扁。

myths.myth_en: A stroke is just a line from one end to the other.
myths.myth_zh: 一筆就是從這頭畫到那頭的線。
myths.fact_en: Every stroke has a start, a middle, and a finish. The tip can hide at the start, run in the middle, and turn back or lift to a point at the end.
myths.fact_zh: 每一筆都有起筆、行筆、收筆：起筆可以藏鋒，行筆走中鋒，收筆可以回鋒，或是提成尖。

tricks.title_en: Press for thick, lift for thin
tricks.body_en: The hairs spread when you press and gather when you lift.
tricks.body_zh: 按下去筆毛散開，提起來筆毛收攏。

tricks.title_en: Keep the tip in the middle
tricks.body_en: An upright handle keeps the tip in the middle of the line.
tricks.body_zh: 筆桿直立，筆尖就在線的中間。

tricks.title_en: Hide it, then bring it back
tricks.body_en: Start against the direction, finish by turning back.
tricks.body_zh: 起筆逆著走，收筆往回收。

tricks.body_en: Hold the brush as if an egg were resting in your palm.

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Old newspaper or a water-writing cloth

steps.en: Dip the brush in the water and wipe it on the edge of the cup so it is wet but not dripping.
steps.zh: 毛筆蘸水，在杯緣刮一刮，濕但不會滴。

steps.en: Draw a horizontal line at an even speed: start light, press down slowly until it is thick, then lift slowly until it is thin again.
steps.zh: 用平均的速度畫一條橫線：先輕輕地，慢慢按到最粗，再慢慢提起來變細。

steps.en: Draw a wave line: press, lift, press, lift. Then draw a vertical line that ends in a fine point, like a hanging needle.
steps.zh: 畫一條波浪線：按、提、按、提。再畫一條豎線，收尾提成細細的尖，像懸著的針。

steps.en: Trade with a partner and guess where they pressed and where they lifted. Write again after the water dries.
steps.zh: 和同學交換，猜猜對方哪裡按、哪裡提。水乾了再寫一次。

activities.tip_en: Water marks fade as they dry, so students can try again and again without wasting ink or paper.
activities.tip_zh: 水痕乾了就消失，學生可以一次又一次地試，不浪費墨也不浪費紙。

activities.title_en: An Egg in the Palm: The Five-Finger Check
activities.title_zh: 掌中握蛋：五指執筆檢查

materials.en: A ping-pong ball or a small ball for each pair
materials.zh: 每兩人一顆乒乓球或小球

materials.en: A cup of water and old newspaper
A checklist with the five characters: 擫、押、鉤、格、抵
materials.zh: 寫著擫、押、鉤、格、抵的檢查表

steps.en: Hold the ball loosely in your palm, then pick up the brush with all five fingers so the ball can stay there.
steps.zh: 掌心輕輕握著球，再用五根手指拿起毛筆，讓球還能留在掌心裡。

steps.en: Your partner checks each finger against the checklist, and that the handle stands upright.
steps.zh: 同學照檢查表一根一根看手指，也看筆桿是不是直立。

steps.en: Put the ball down, keep the hollow palm, and write 十 with water: the horizontal first, then the vertical.
steps.zh: 把球放下，掌心保持空空的，用清水寫「十」：先橫後豎。

steps.en: Switch roles. Talk about it: what changes when the handle leans?
steps.zh: 交換角色。討論：筆桿斜了，線條有什麼不一樣？

activities.tip_en: The ball is only a reminder of a hollow palm; take it away before writing for real. Left-handed students can mirror every step.
activities.tip_zh: 球只是用來提醒「掌虛」，真正寫字前要拿走。用左手的學生，每一步左右相反就好。

sources.en: Center tip (中鋒, also 正鋒): however the brush turns, the tip stays in the middle of the stroke
sources.zh: 中鋒：寫毛筆字時，不論如何運轉，筆鋒均保持在筆畫的中間，也稱「正鋒」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「中鋒」

sources.en: Side tip (側鋒): the tip is not in the middle of the stroke but leans to one side
sources.zh: 側鋒：運筆時筆心不在筆畫中央，筆鋒偏側
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「側鋒」

sources.en: Hiding the tip (藏鋒): the tip is hidden and not shown
sources.zh: 藏鋒：筆鋒藏而不露
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「藏鋒」

sources.en: Returning the tip (回鋒): at the end of a stroke, the brush turns back
sources.zh: 回鋒：行筆至筆畫的盡頭，反向回收
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「回鋒」

sources.en: Start, middle, and finish of a stroke; the horizontal, the dew-drop vertical, and the hanging-needle vertical as basic strokes taught in elementary school
sources.zh: 運筆過程：起筆、行筆、收筆；基本筆法教學：橫、垂露豎、懸針豎
sources.src: 宜蘭縣國小書法教學資料（ilc.edu.tw）

sources.en: The five-character grip 擫、押、鉤、格、抵, recorded as obtained by Lu Xisheng of the Tang dynasty; the job of each finger; fingers firm and palm hollow, “like holding an egg”
sources.zh: 「唐陸希聲得撥鐙法凡五字，曰擫、押、鈎、格、抵」（楊賓語）；五指各自的用力方式；指實掌虛、「形同握卵」
sources.src: 鄭國瑞〈楊賓之書學觀〉，《東海大學圖書館館訊》新 89 期（2010）

sources.en: The five-finger grip: thumb, index, and middle fingers hold the brush and keep the handle straight; the little finger supports the ring finger; the palm is shaped as if hiding an egg
sources.zh: 五指執筆：大拇指、食指、中指握住並保持筆桿直；小指托住無名指；掌心像藏著一顆蛋
sources.src: Lee & Lee, International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (2021)

sources.en: 心正筆正: “Using the brush depends on the heart; when the heart is upright, the brush is upright” (Liu Gongquan to Emperor Muzong, Old Book of Tang)
sources.zh: 心正筆正：「用筆在心，心正則筆正」（《舊唐書．柳公綽傳》）
sources.src: 教育部《成語典》「心正筆正」

sources.en: “上改容，知其筆諫也”: the emperor's face changed, understanding the advice
sources.zh: 「上改容，知其筆諫也」
sources.src: 《舊唐書》卷一百六十五（維基文庫）

sources.en: 鐵畫銀鉤: from Ouyang Xun's On Using the Brush (“剛則鐵畫，媚若銀鉤”); Youxue Qionglin uses it for Wang Xizhi's writing
sources.zh: 鐵畫銀鉤：語本唐歐陽詢〈用筆論〉；《幼學瓊林》「鐵畫銀鉤，王羲之之字法」
sources.src: 教育部《成語典》「鐵畫銀鉤」

sources.en: 力透紙背: the force of the brush reaches through to the back of the paper; from Yan Zhenqing's record of Zhang Xu's brush methods
sources.zh: 力透紙背：運筆的力量穿透到紙的另一面；語本唐顏真卿〈張長史十二意筆法記〉
